traits.ribs.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Echinocactus polycephalus: plants branched from the base forming compact mounds of 2-50(-130) branches; stems gray-green to yellow-green, spheric to short cylindric, 15-40 × (9-)15-30 cm; ribs 11-25, the crests sharp, with flat sides. Spines 10-19 per areole, straight to curved but not hooked, often twisted, red to straw coloured, aging gray, flattened to abaxially ridged, nearly obscuring the stem, glabrous to canescent; radial spines 6-14 per areole; central spines 4, the abaxial frequently longest, straight to somewhat recurved. Flowers 5.5-5.8 × 4-6 cm; inner tepals bright yellow; stigma lobes bright yellow. Fruits ovoid, hidden by hairs, drying to a tan shell, 15-40 mm. Var. polycephalus: stems gray-green; spines red to gray, canescent; flowering Jul-Aug. Colours by hand from the words; heights from its stems' 15-40 cm.

traits.radial_spine_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Echinocactus: stems gray-blue, gray-green, yellow-green or grass green, flat-topped spheric to short cylindric, the apical region appearing copiously woolly; ribs very prominent; spines conspicuously annulate-ridged, rigid; radial spines 5-14 per areole, straight to curved, 2-5 cm; central spines 1-4, straight to curved. Flowers near the stem apex, broadly funnelform to nearly salverform; ovary scaly, spineless, copiously woolly, with white or pale tan hairs from the areoles hiding the ovary and flower tube; stigma lobes 6-14(-17). Fruits many scaled, the axils of the scales copiously woolly (the wool hiding the fruit except in E. texensis), spineless; floral remnant persistent. The species: fruits hidden by hairs, drying to a tan shell. Its radials the genus's longest; the carpels as many as the stigma lobes; colours by hand from the words.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from the flora's words: a compact mound of up to 50 grey-green heads, leaning out from the middle, crowned with white wool and yellow flowers in summer. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: A rough head height: about 30 cm by 50 years. Wide tolerance.

appearance.note: Rib depth and sharpness by eye for the flora's sharp, flat-sided crests; areoles about 2.5 cm apart by eye (the flora gives no spacing); spine widths for its flattened, stout spines, the abaxial central the main one.

taxon.note: Scientific names as WCVP v16 accepts them, common names as the Flora of North America gives them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
